items.title: Trump’s new press secretary admits failing bar exam
items.description: New White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia acknowledged on Thursday that she had failed the bar exam, a prerequisite for practicing law in the United States, as her credentials face scrutiny. Zacharia has described herself as a lawyer during television appearances and on social media, and listed herself as general counsel of a California-based conservative nonprofit. But the legal credentials of the press secretary, who President Donald Trump appointed last week, were called into question after she gave an inconclusive answer about where she had passed the bar exam. The 41-year-old graduated from Pepperdine University’s law school in 2011, but obtaining a law degree does not automatically qualify someone to practice law. In a Fox News interview on Thursday, host Sean Hannity asked Zacharia: “You took the bar exam, but you didn’t pass the bar exam, correct?” “Yes,” she responded. In a separate interview with conservative media outlet Real America’s Voice on Thursday, Zacharia said she had registered to take the bar exam but was “distracted and overwhelmed” by plans to move to China with her husband. “The results are somewhat inconsequential because I knew I wouldn’t need the bar in China,” she said. Foreign nationals cannot sit China’s bar exam, although they can undertake certain legal work at Chinese law firms. Hannity later asked Zacharia if she had ever taken the bar exam a second time, to which she said: “I did not.” “I had four kids in six years,” she said. “It was never my intent to go into the practice of law.” Zacharia said on Real America’s Voice that “many people in the field” had assured her that she could “label myself a lawyer,” given her law degree and experience in business law gained in China, where she worked at a Beijing law firm. She added that she could “provide legal analysis, not legal advice.” “I was very careful how I executed this.” The Campaign for Accountability, a political ethics organization, called on Wednesday for the California Bar Association to launch an investigation. “In California, calling yourself a lawyer without a license isn’t puffery; it’s a crime,” the organization said in a press release. Zacharia held her first White House press briefing on Tuesday with an unusually short press conference, answering questions from only three journalists. She succeeded Karoline Leavitt, a loyal Trump supporter and often combative press secretary, who stepped down in August to care for her young children. AFP The post Trump’s new press secretary admits failing bar exam appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Rivers DPO, DO suspended over renovation of police post by suspected cultists
items.description: By Davies Iheamnachor, PORT HARCOURT A Divisional Police Officer (DPO) of a station in Rivers State has been suspended alongside some other serving officers of his post for reportedly allowing cultists to renovate their facility. The Rivers State Police Comand disclosed this worrisome development in a statement by its Public Relations Officer, Blessing Agabe, an Assistant Superintendent of Police, in Port Harcourt, Friday. It was learned that some cultists in Abuloma Community of Okirika, but in Port Harcourt City Local Government Area, had funded the renovation of a police outpost in their area and that the development was exposed when the cultists visited to celebrate their contribution to the force. Agabe, however, in the statement, condemned the renovation by the cultists, noting that the development happened at Abuloma area of Port Harcourt. Agabe noted that the act was capable of denting the image of the force, adding that a police station is a public facility used to tackle issues of criminality and cannot be used by criminals to get validation. She said, “The Rivers State Police Command has taken cognisance of a trending social media report and circulating video alleging that suspected cultists renovated the Abuloma Police Outpost and visited the facility on Thursday, October 15, 2026, to celebrate the completion of the renovation. “The Command strongly condemns any action or association capable of compromising the integrity, discipline and professional standards of the Nigeria Police Force or conferring legitimacy, recognition or acceptance on suspected cult groups or other unlawful organisations. Police facilities are public institutions established for the protection of citizens and the enforcement of law and must not become platforms through which criminal groups seek public validation or influence. “Under the leadership of CP Olugbenga A. Adepoju, PSC, MNIPS, FCAI, the Command maintains zero tolerance for criminality and any conduct that undermines public confidence in the Police.” Agabe revealed that the DPO in charge of the station and DO have been relieved of their duties and are currently under investigation. She said, “Consequently, the Divisional Police Officer (DPO) in charge of Abuloma Division and the Divisional Officer overseeing the affected Police Outpost have been queried and relieved of their duties pending investigation. “Furthermore, the Commissioner of Police has ordered a full investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and the veracity of the allegations.’ The PPRO noted that the investigation would unravel the identities and backgrounds of the individuals or groups who financed or facilitated the renovation, the police officers who authorised or approved the project, and the extent of any involvement by police personnel. “The Command welcomes legitimate community support for improving police facilities, consistent with Section 26(1)(d) of the Nigeria Police Act 2020, which provides for gifts and contributions to the Police General Fund. “However, such support must not compromise police independence, professional standards or security. The investigation will establish whether the necessary approvals were obtained and appropriate checks conducted on those who financed or facilitated the renovation,” she added. The post Rivers DPO, DO suspended over renovation of police post by suspected cultists appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Un message militaire crypté sur ordre de Napoléon déchiffré après plus de deux siècles grâce à l’IA
items.description: Un message militaire code, compose d'une vingtaine de lignes de symboles, de chiffres et de lettres, vient de livrer ses secrets apres plus de deux siecles. La lettre, adressee au general francais Auguste de Marmont, detaille les positions des armees francaises et alliees en Europe. Si certaines references historiques la dataient de 1807, une nouvelle analyse a permis de la situer en mars 1809, a la veille de la reprise de la guerre entre la France napoleonienne et l'Autriche. Contrairement a ce que peuvent laisser entendre certains titres, le document n'a pas ete ecrit directement par Napoleon Bonaparte. Il a ete transmis par Eugene de Beauharnais, beau-fils de l'empereur et vice-roi d'Italie, sur instruction de Napoleon. Le 16 mars 1809, Napoleon lui avait demande d'informer Marmont, alors a la tete des troupes stationnees en Dalmatie, de la disposition des forces francaises et alliees. La communication devait etre chiffree et confiee a un officier juge fiable. Le message a ete reproduit dans une revue militaire francaise en 1969, mais sa cle de chiffrement n'avait pas ete retrouvee. Il est ainsi reste sans decryptage complet pendant 217 ans. Son dechiffrement supposait notamment de reconstituer un systeme complexe de substitution, dans lequel plusieurs signes pouvaient representer une meme lettre. La faible resolution de la reproduction et l'absence de transcription complete avaient egalement complique son etude. Selon les medias francais, notamment Euronews, l'ingenieur americain Carter Church, specialiste de l'intelligence artificielle (IA) au sein de l'entreprise de cybersecurite SentinelOne, a finalement resolu l'enigme avec le modele GPT-6 Astra d'OpenAI. Le travail de decryptage effectue par le modele a pris environ six heures. L'intelligence artificielle accelere la cryptanalyse historique Pour parvenir a ce resultat, l'IA a d'abord analyse l'image du document, identifie les signes repetes, puis recherche les correspondances permettant de reconstituer le texte en francais. Le texte obtenu a ensuite ete confronte a des documents historiques, notamment aux instructions donnees par Napoleon en mars 1809. Le contenu dechiffre decrit les positions de plusieurs armees, dont les forces bavaroises, polonaises et saxonnes, ainsi que les mouvements militaires anticipes face a l'Autriche. Il confirme en grande partie des informations deja presentes dans la correspondance connue de Napoleon, tout en permettant de reconstituer le contenu de cette lettre particuliere. Carter Church a egalement fait verifier son travail par Satoshi Tomokiyo, un chercheur japonais qui tient un inventaire en ligne des codes historiques non resolus. Cette verification a contribue a confirmer la solution et a corriger la datation precedemment attribuee au document. Les methodes traditionnelles de cryptanalyse permettent parfois de resoudre de telles enigmes, mais exigent souvent un investissement considerable en temps et en expertise. L'IA offre la possibilite de tester rapidement des hypotheses, de traiter des images complexes et de comparer les resultats avec de grandes quantites de donnees. Des archives anciennes aux manuscrits fragiles Le decryptage de cette lettre s'inscrit dans un mouvement plus large d'utilisation de l'IA pour l'etude du patrimoine historique. En Italie, des chercheurs analysent par rayons X les papyrus d'Herculanum, carbonises lors de l'eruption du Vesuve en 79 apres J.-C., afin d'en lire virtuellement le contenu sans risquer de detruire ces documents fragiles. D'autres projets utilisent l'IA pour transcrire des millions de pages de manuscrits hebraïques ou des milliers de documents medievaux conserves dans les archives de Notre-Dame de Paris. Ces outils permettent d'exploiter des corpus dont l'analyse manuelle aurait necessite des decennies. Si ces avancees ouvrent de nouvelles perspectives pour les historiens, elles suscitent aussi des interrogations chez les passionnes de cryptographie, pour qui la resolution d'une enigme repose traditionnellement sur de longues recherches personnelles. L'IA ne resout pas tous les codes, notamment lorsque les donnees disponibles sont insuffisantes, mais elle transforme deja les methodes d'etude des documents historiques.

items.title: ‘We have been used and dumped’ – NDC’s James Agbey warns over grassroots neglect
items.description: An operative of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), James Agbey, has warned that the party risks alienating its grassroots supporters unless government appointees address concerns about neglect and a lack of economic opportunities. In a statement dated Friday, October 16, Mr Agbey accused appointees of overlooking activists and cadres who worked to secure the party’s return to power in the 2024 elections. “The feeling out there at the base is that ‘we have been used and dumped’,” he said. Mr Agbey claimed that many party activists were struggling with unemployment and financial hardship, while some appointees were prioritising relatives and close associates over those who supported the party during its years in opposition. “Everything seems to have changed after the elections. Appointees are now prioritising their families and close allies, some of whom were not even part of the struggle,” he alleged. He said the concerns required practical intervention rather than occasional handouts or promises of future support. “All that these party activists are asking for is opportunities to be able to fend for themselves,” he stated. Mr Agbey urged government appointees to engage with the party’s support base and take concrete steps to address their concerns. He warned that unresolved grievances could weaken loyalty and lead dissatisfied activists to turn against the government in a future election. “Our support for the NDC must not be taken for granted,” he cautioned. The statement did not provide figures to substantiate his claim that the party’s support base was dwindling or identify the appointees accused of favouring relatives and associates. Mr Agbey nevertheless maintained that the leadership needed to act urgently to prevent growing frustration from damaging the party’s electoral prospects. “I call for urgent action or we will have ourselves to blame come the electioneering season,” he said.

items.title: Masques et marionnettes : Un patrimoine vivant à transmettre
items.description: © Internet Porteurs de récits, de croyances et de valeurs sociales, les masques et marionnettes occupent une place essentielle dans le patrimoine culturel malien. Reconnue par l’UNESCO, la tradition de Markala reste toutefois confrontée au défi de la transmission. Les masques et les marionnettes sont bien plus que des objets sculptés ou des personnages de spectacle. Ils racontent l’histoire des communautés, transmettent des valeurs et traduisent une vision du monde dans laquelle les êtres humains, les animaux et les forces invisibles sont étroitement liés. Dans les sociétés traditionnelles, ces pratiques accompagnent les cérémonies et les rassemblements communautaires. Elles associent sculpture, danse, chant, musique et représentation théâtrale, tout en faisant circuler des connaissances héritées des générations précédentes. Selon le maître marionnettiste Yaya Coulibaly, leurs origines remontent à l’ancienne relation entre les humains, les animaux sauvages et les esprits associés aux forêts, aux cours d’eau et aux collines sacrées. « La première marionnette est la jeune fille appelée mɛrɛn », explique-t-il. Chaque masque et chaque marionnette possède une signification. Le lion symbolise la puissance et l’autorité, tandis que la vache, appelée misi, apparaît dans des représentations qui dénoncent certains travers de la société. Transmission Les marionnettes collectives, connues sous le nom de kalakakɔnɔ sogow, reproduisent les comportements humains à travers des scènes symboliques. Les spectacles rappellent l’importance de la solidarité, de l’honnêteté et du respect des règles sociales. Pour Yaya Coulibaly, le recul de ces pratiques tient d’abord à la rupture de la transmission entre les générations. Autrefois, les anciens enseignaient aux jeunes les techniques de fabrication, les récits et la signification des représentations. « Aujourd’hui, cette transmission devient difficile, notamment à cause du désintérêt de certains jeunes, du manque de moyens financiers et de l’évolution des modes de vie », observe-t-il. Les changements religieux conduisent aussi à l’abandon de certaines traditions. L’insécurité empêche l’organisation de manifestations culturelles dans plusieurs localités, notamment à Markala. Sans formation des jeunes, soutien aux artistes et sensibilisation des communautés, certains savoir-faire pourraient disparaître avec leurs détenteurs. L’inscription en 2014 de la sortie des masques et marionnettes de Markala sur la Liste représentative du Patrimoine culturel immatériel de l’Humanité constitue une reconnaissance, mais elle ne suffit pas à assurer durablement leur continuité. « Pour préserver ce patrimoine, il faut encourager la transmission, valoriser le travail des marionnettistes et donner davantage de place à ces expressions culturelles dans nos événements et nos espaces éducatifs », conclut Yaya Coulibaly. Joseph Amara Dembélé

items.title: Ghana defender Marvin Senaya begins training ahead of comeback
items.description: Black Stars fullback Marvin Senaya has returned to light training on grass as he aims to return to competitive action following a muscle injury sustained during the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Senaya suffered a hamstring injury during Ghana’s Round of 32 clash against Colombia in July and has been out since the new season commenced. The injury has forced the Ghanaian fullback to miss the opening seven league matches for AJ Auxerre. His return to on-pitch running shows progression in his recovery. However, a definite return to competitive action has not been confirmed. Senaya was a standout player for Ghana during the 2026 World Cup, earning praise for his performances during the campaign. His eventual return to match fitness will be a bright spot for Auxerre, while the Black Stars will also hope to utilise the defender for upcoming international fixtures once he full recovers.

items.title: Sondages en France : Glucksmann déjà écarté du second tour de la présidentielle
items.description: Un barometre PresiTrack realise par OpinionWay pour Les echos, publie le 15 octobre, a donne « pour la premiere fois » Raphael Glucksmann au second tour de la presidentielle de 2027, volant la vedette a Jean-Luc Melenchon comme principal challenger de Marine Le Pen, qui conserve une tres nette avance dans les intentions de vote. Quelques jours apres sa victoire a la primaire dite « sociale-democrate », celui que Bruno Retailleau decrit comme ayant « le charisme d'un horodateur en panne » est ainsi credite de 16 % des intentions de vote, contre 15 % pour le dernier tribun de la vie politique francaise. Les deux hommes de gauche sont neanmoins donnes au coude a coude, a 15 %, en cas de presence d'edouard Philippe en lieu et place de Gabriel Attal. Le maire du Havre est lui-meme credite de 15 % des intentions de vote par ce sondage PresiTrack. Un « effet boost », selon un sondeur « Il y a vraiment un effet boost en faveur de Raphael Glucksmann. Il est meme plus fort qu'attendu puisque le mouvement lyceen affaiblit les deux candidats du bloc central, Gabriel Attal et edouard Philippe », a declare au quotidien d'information economique le vice-president d'OpinionWay, Bruno Jeanbart. « Fin 2016, Benoît Hamon, vainqueur de la primaire socialiste, avait, lui aussi, connu une forte hausse dans les sondages avant de s'effondrer par la suite et de finir a 6 % », a toutefois tempere Les echos. Le 11 octobre, apres avoir ete donne gagnant par un sondage publie le jour meme de l'ouverture des votes – qui s'etaient etires sur une journee supplementaire apres l'annonce d'une cyberattaque contre la plateforme – Raphael Glucksmann avait remporte cette primaire de la gauche avec plus de 66 % des suffrages. a l'issue de cette annonce, cet ancien conseiller de l'ex-president georgien Mikheïl Saakachvili avait eu droit a une couverture mediatique digne d'une victoire a une presidentielle, des journalistes prenant en chasse son scooter a travers les rues de Paris.

items.title: Chelsea : Reece James opéré du genou, son retour reste incertain
items.description: Le capitaine de Chelsea, Reece James, a subi avec succès une opération du genou, a annoncé vendredi le club londonien. Aucune date de retour à la compétition n’a pour l’instant été communiquée. Nouveau coup dur pour Chelsea. Le capitaine des Blues, Reece James, a été opéré du genou à la suite d’une blessure contractée à l’entraînement. Le club de Premier League a annoncé vendredi que l’intervention chirurgicale s’était déroulée avec succès, sans toutefois préciser la durée de son indisponibilité. Âgé de 26 ans, l’international anglais avait manqué la rencontre face à Bournemouth, remportée 5-1 samedi dernier à Stamford Bridge. Des examens médicaux réalisés après sa blessure ont confirmé la nécessité d’une opération, selon le communiqué du club. Chelsea a précisé que le joueur avait déjà entamé sa phase de rétablissement et serait suivi par le service médical du club à Cobham durant sa rééducation. Capable d’évoluer au poste de latéral droit comme au milieu défensif, Reece James avait également manqué la défaite de Chelsea face à Brentford (3-0), avant le succès contre Bournemouth. Son absence intervient alors que les Blues occupent la sixième place de Premier League, avant leur déplacement sur la pelouse d’Everton samedi. Le club londonien devra désormais suivre l’évolution de la convalescence de son capitaine, dont la date de retour sur les terrains reste inconnue. The post Chelsea : Reece James opéré du genou, son retour reste incertain appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Financement public : L’option FMI se précise
items.description: © Internet Après la mission conduite du 5 au 9 octobre, le Mali et le Fonds monétaire international poursuivent leurs échanges en vue d’un programme appuyé par une Facilité élargie de crédit (FEC). Encore à préparer, cet accord pourrait permettre de diversifier les ressources et de réduire la pression du financement intérieur. La visite du FMI n’a pas débouché sur l’ouverture de négociations. Le ministère de l’Économie et des Finances annonce la transmission d’informations complémentaires et des visioconférences. Aucun montant, calendrier ou engagement définitif n’a encore été arrêté. Les besoins de financement de l’État restent élevés. Selon la Direction générale de la dette publique, le Trésor a mobilisé 724,23 milliards de francs CFA sur le marché régional de l’UEMOA au premier semestre 2026. Fin juin, la dette intérieure représentait 52,9% de l’encours total, contre 47,1% pour la dette extérieure. Le taux d’endettement s’établissait à 38,3% du PIB. Le niveau global est inférieur au plafond communautaire de 70%, mais la structure de la dette compte. Dans son dernier rapport sur le Mali, le FMI relevait qu’environ 1 285 milliards de francs CFA d’obligations régionales et de prêts syndiqués arrivaient à échéance en 2026, presque deux fois plus qu’en 2025. Le recours soutenu aux banques et au marché régional alourdit le service de la dette et peut réduire les ressources disponibles pour financer les entreprises. Un relais concessionnel Une FEC offrirait des ressources à des conditions plus favorables et sur une durée plus longue que les émissions à court terme. Elle pourrait aussi compléter les financements déjà obtenus auprès de la Banque mondiale, de la BAD et de la BOAD. Selon la même source, sept accords totalisant 190,89 milliards de francs CFA ont été signés au premier semestre, dont 185,88 milliards sous forme de prêts. Le futur programme prolongerait les réformes engagées dans le cadre du programme de référence achevé en 2026 : mobilisation des recettes intérieures, numérisation fiscale, contrôle des marchés publics, suivi des entreprises publiques et protection des dépenses sociales. Le FMI prévoit une croissance de 5,5% en 2026, contre 6,3% dans les projections officielles. L’accord reste toutefois à construire. Son intérêt économique tiendra autant aux ressources mobilisées qu’à sa capacité à diminuer le coût du financement, préserver les investissements publics et éviter que les besoins de l’État ne pèsent davantage sur le crédit destiné au secteur privé.

items.title: Elon Musk unveils Tesla’s ‘flying’ car
items.description: Tesla CEO Elon Musk unveiled what he described as a “flying” car, equipped with thrusters, during a livestreamed event at his SpaceX rocket company’s facility on Thursday. Technical and regulatory challenges have so far prevented the much-hyped flying car sector from getting off the ground. Musk revealed his new Roadster sports car during a launch event at a SpaceX test facility in Texas. During the demo, which was livestreamed on Tesla’s X account, the car launched from a steep ramp and landed on its wheels. “Flying cars are real,” Musk said during the event. He added that the vehicle’s “success is not guaranteed” but that “it will probably work.” Musk said the car was equipped with “ultra high-pressure air tanks” to propel itself into the air. The tech billionaire described the development as “what happens when you have a collaboration with the world’s best car company and the world’s best rocket company,” referring to Tesla and SpaceX. The vehicle would go into production in 2028, he said. American aviation pioneer Glenn Curtiss debuted the first flying car prototype in 1917. But successful designs have become more seriously contemplated only in recent years as electric motors and high-performance batteries have advanced. AFP The post Elon Musk unveils Tesla’s ‘flying’ car appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Families of children killed in Peshawar school roof collapse demand justice
items.description: The families of children killed in a roof collapse in Peshawar’s Afridi Abad area called for “justice” on Friday, the day after more than 30 people, including students and a female teacher, were killed in the incident . “The parents of all these children must receive justice,” tailor Muhammad Wahab, who lost his 11-year-old nephew Hammad in the accident, told AFP . “I appeal to our rulers,” he said, adding that Hammad had been “doing well in school” before the tragedy. Dozens of people gathered on Friday outside the school to mourn the children who were killed in the collapse, which officials blamed on dilapidated infrastructure. One grief-stricken father showed AFP a picture on his mobile phone of his young daughter, dressed in red and gold, who lost her life. Another parent, Asadullah, said he lost a son, nephew, and three other close relatives in the tragedy. “The children were good students and often achieved top positions in their classes,” he told AFP . “They happily went to school every day.” Residents and rescuers described chaotic scenes in the aftermath of Thursday’s collapse, as people scrambled to pull children out from under the rubble. A man named Sohail told AFP that “everyone began screaming in panic” when his niece, who had escaped the building, arrived home to tell them it had collapsed. “When I arrived at the scene, I saw around 10 to 15 children trapped beneath the rubble, with debris piled up to their necks. We quickly pulled them out,” he said. Children try to peek through the sealed entrance of school a day after its roof collapsed killing several students in Peshawar on October 16, 2026. — AFP Soon after the incident, the provincial chief secretary on Thursday constituted a fact-finding committee to probe the incident and tasked it with submitting a report within seven days. Building and roof collapses are common in Pakistan, often attributed to poor safety standards and the use of substandard construction materials. The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP) held it was “not an accident but a preventable failure,” and recalled a similar incident in Lahore in June, which claimed the lives of 14 students. Audit report of private school buildings in KP to be submitted in 4 days: Governor Kundi Meanwhile, speaking at a press conference on Friday, KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi said those responsible for negligence in the school roof collapse would be held accountable, adding that legal action would be taken within 15 days and those found at fault would be punished. “Until they are punished, schools will open in houses every day. We are also going to audit government and private schools,” Kundi claimed. “In four to five days, building audit reports of all private schools in the province will be submitted to us.” He added he had given (officials) 15 days to submit reports on government schools as well. “After the audit, if an incident happens, the auditor will be punished,” Kundi asserted. Governor Kundi also announced compensation of Rs1 million for each bereaved family and Rs300,000 for each injured person. He said the school owner had been arrested, and that action will be taken against other people involved in the incident. “On one hand, we are fighting a war against terrorism; on the other hand, those who play with the lives of children do not deserve any concession,” Kundi said. People pray for students killed after a roof collapsed at a school, in Peshawar on October 16, 2026. — AFP Meanwhile, Samar Haroon Bilour, who is the adviser to the KP governor on information and public relations, in a televised message, urged residents to share videos of schools in poor condition in their areas, saying an inspection team had been dispatched to Mardan’s Gumbat village after a video showing a school in a dilapidated condition was received. “Since yesterday, many of my brothers and sisters from different areas in KP are sending me messages through WhatsApp, Facebook, X, showing schools in their areas,” Bilour said. “I request all of you to stand with us in this difficult time. The Governor Advisory Council has given four days’ time for inspection of schools. I request you to check schools in your area and share videos with us,” she added.

items.title: Joyce Bawah Mogtari urges women leaders to build strong support networks
items.description: Senior Presidential Advisor and Aide to President John Dramani Mahama, Joyce Bawah Mogtari, has urged women in leadership to surround themselves with people who will support their growth, defend them against unfair treatment and offer honest advice. In a Facebook post on Friday, October 16, she reflected on a discussion with former Electoral Commission Chairperson Charlotte Osei at the Obaasima Conference, where the challenges women encounter in leadership featured prominently. Ms Bawah Mogtari said the conversation reinforced the importance of having a dependable support system in workplaces where women’s abilities and achievements are often questioned. She said a genuine support network should go beyond public expressions of solidarity to include people willing to speak up against injustice, offer constructive criticism and celebrate the progress of others without feeling threatened. Such relationships, she noted, can make a significant difference in how women navigate the pressures of leadership. Ms Bawah Mogtari said the Obaasima Conference should provide a platform for women to share their experiences, learn from one another and develop meaningful connections. She stressed that while leadership can be difficult for women, having trusted people to rely on can make the journey more manageable and rewarding.

items.title: Bawumia engages GUTA over import duties, VAT and rising business costs
items.description: Former Vice President and New Patriotic Party (NPP) flagbearer for the 2028 elections, Dr Mahamudu Bawumia, has held talks with the Ghana Union of Traders’ Associations (GUTA) on challenges affecting traders, including high import duties, rising demurrage charges and the cost of doing business. In a Facebook post on Friday, October 16, Dr Bawumia said executives and representatives of GUTA outlined concerns over high import duties, the reported increase in VAT for informal sector operators to 20%, limited access to EXIM loans, high shop rents and goodwill payments, as well as foreign nationals taking over aspects of the retail trade. He described the engagement as productive and said the association also presented proposals to address some of the challenges. The discussions also focused on how Ghana could move from dependence on imported goods towards local production. Dr Bawumia said he and the traders explored incentives that could encourage businesses to manufacture more goods locally, potentially creating jobs and expanding opportunities for Ghanaian businesses. He thanked GUTA for the engagement and the ideas it presented, saying the discussions had provided useful insights into the difficulties facing traders. The meeting forms part of conversations on possible policy measures to improve the business environment, ease operational pressures and support domestic production and private-sector growth.

items.title: Fuel prices begin to fall as Star Oil cuts petrol to GH¢16.45
items.description: Some oil marketing companies (OMCs) have begun reducing fuel prices at the pumps as the second pricing window for October takes effect. Star Oil reduced its petrol price from GH¢16.64 to GH¢16.45 per litre, effective 8am on Friday, October 16, 2026. Other OMCs have told JoyBusiness they intend to review their prices, although some say they will monitor competitors before making adjustments. While motorists could benefit from lower petrol and diesel prices, users of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) face a projected increase of more than 18%. The Chamber of Oil Marketing Companies expects LPG to sell at about GH¢20.60 per kilogramme. Reasons for the adjustments The Chamber attributed the projected price movements to developments in the international petroleum market, exchange-rate pressures, and recent government interventions. According to its report, average crude oil prices rose by 2.03% to US$126.73 per barrel for the October 16 pricing window. The Chamber linked the increase to renewed supply concerns, citing uncertainty over a proposed US-backed energy ceasefire involving Ukraine and fresh attacks on Saudi Arabia amid the conflict with Iran. Despite the rise in crude prices, refined petroleum products recorded mixed movements. International LPG prices increased by 7.77%, while diesel and petrol prices fell by 6.68% and 3.93%, respectively. Meanwhile, the cedi depreciated by 1.61% against the US dollar, reaching an average bank rate of GH¢11.8222 between September 26 and October 11, 2026. The Chamber said the local currency had lost more than 11% against the dollar since the beginning of the year, with seasonal import demand and higher energy costs continuing to exert pressure. The weaker cedi is expected to limit how much of the decline in international petrol and diesel prices is passed on to consumers. Competition and the NPA’s price floor Some OMCs say competition will influence the timing and extent of their price adjustments. However, their pricing decisions must also comply with the National Petroleum Authority’s minimum price requirements. Market information available to JoyBusiness puts the petrol price floor at GH¢16.09 per litre and the LPG floor at GH¢13.87 per kilogramme. These floors represent minimum selling prices, not the pump prices that every company must charge. Actual prices may therefore vary among OMCs.

items.title: GoldBod supplies banks with US$282m in weekly forex sales
items.description: The Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) says it sold US$282 million to commercial banks through its foreign exchange (FX) sales programme on Tuesday, October 13, and Thursday, October 15, 2026, as part of efforts to increase dollar supply to Ghana’s domestic market. In a statement, the Board said US$197 million was sold on Tuesday, followed by an additional US$85 million on Thursday. GoldBod explained that the transactions were conducted through its digital GoldBod GoFX platform to make foreign exchange earned from Ghana’s gold resources available to participating commercial banks. GoldBod said the programme is backed by Section 2(b) of the Ghana Gold Board Act, 2025 (Act 1140), which provides for the Board to supply foreign exchange to the country. According to the Board, participating banks submit requests for US dollars through the platform, with allocations made under the real-time monitoring of the Bank of Ghana. The Board reiterated that the arrangement constitutes spot FX sales rather than forex trading. It explained that it sells dollars earned from its gold operations to commercial banks in exchange for cedis, which are then used to finance its gold purchases. GoldBod said the supply of dollars to commercial banks helps businesses access foreign currency for imports, international payments and other legitimate obligations. The Board added that improved FX availability could help ease pressure on the cedi and imported costs, while supporting market stability and the financing of its gold purchasing operations.

items.title: Marché Gambie de Colobane : la capitale du textile et du consommer local
items.description: À Colobane, le secteur textile incarne concrètement la souveraineté économique et culturelle du Sénégal. Vendeurs de tissus, couturiers et jeunes créatrices y font vivre une chaîne de valeur locale qui rend la mode sur mesure accessible, tout en favorisant la création d’emplois et la valorisation du savoir-faire sénégalais. Au cœur du quartier populaire de Colobane, là où la poussière ocre des allées se mêle à l’effervescence permanente de la capitale sénégalaise, le marché Gambie s’anime dès les premières lueurs de l’aube. Entre les klaxons, les négociations des clients et les étoffes aux couleurs chatoyantes, cet espace marchand s’impose comme l’un des hauts lieux du textile et de la mode à Dakar. À l’heure où les discours sur la souveraineté économique et la promotion du « made in Sénégal » prennent de l’ampleur, l’activité de Colobane illustre le potentiel de la production locale. Des tissus achetés sur place aux vêtements confectionnés dans les ateliers voisins, toute une chaîne d’acteurs contribue à habiller les Sénégalais, en proposant des tenues adaptées à leurs goûts et à leurs moyens. Pour comprendre cette dynamique, il faut s’enfoncer dans les allées animées du marché Gambie. Sous les toiles tendues, les étals dévoilent une grande variété de couleurs, de motifs et de matières. Dans la boutique de Bassirou Kébé, l’activité ne faiblit pas. Des employés déroulent de lourdes pièces de tissu sur les comptoirs, tandis que les clients examinent les étoffes, vérifient leur qualité et négocient les prix. PDG de l’établissement Wa Keur Serigne Bassirou Kébé et Frères, le commerçant met en avant la diversité des produits proposés. « On vend des tissus en lin, du coton suisse, du coton fleurette, des tissus brodés. On vend en gros comme au détail. Nos clients viennent de partout dans la sous-région, notamment du Mali et de la Guinée. On n’a pas de problème pour les matières premières », explique-t-il. Au-delà de la diversité des tissus, les prix constituent un argument commercial important. Dans la boutique, les vendeurs mesurent les étoffes au mètre, tandis que certaines ventes se font au kilo. Dans un contexte marqué par les préoccupations liées au coût de la vie, cette offre permet aux couturiers et aux créateurs de s’approvisionner à des tarifs qu’ils jugent avantageux. Bassirou Kébé détaille les prix pratiqués : « Les tissus en lin sont vendus à 1 500 francs CFA le mètre, les tissus brodés à 2 500 francs CFA. Pour les tissus pour hommes, il y en a à 3 000 et à 4 000 francs CFA, selon la qualité. Nous vendons au mètre comme au kilo. Les clients préfèrent venir ici plutôt que d’importer des vêtements déjà confectionnés. C’est moins cher pour eux. » Cette accessibilité attire notamment les couturières et les jeunes entrepreneures qui développent leur activité grâce au commerce en ligne. C’est le cas de Ndeye Marie Faye, qui dispose d’un atelier à Thiaroye. Venue renouveler son stock, elle achète ses tissus à Colobane avant de les transformer en tenues destinées à ses clients. « Je fais de la vente en ligne et j’ai mon atelier à Thiaroye. Je viens toujours acheter les tissus ici pour les coudre ensuite, puisque je suis couturière. Je préfère venir acheter ici plutôt que d’importer », confie-t-elle. Même conviction chez Marie Renée Sylla, fondatrice de la boutique OLGA SHOP. Pour cette entrepreneure, le choix de la confection locale répond à une logique à la fois économique et culturelle. « Aujourd’hui, au Sénégal, on a compris que notre créativité vaut de l’or. Pourquoi porter ce que le monde nous envoie quand on peut coudre nous-mêmes ? », interroge-t-elle. Pour elle, la mode locale représente également un levier de développement et de création d’emplois. « Coudre ici, c’est donner du travail à la jeunesse, c’est aussi porter notre culture. Avant, on courait derrière les vêtements importés, mais maintenant les Sénégalais sont fiers. Ils veulent du sur-mesure, une coupe qui respecte leur corps », souligne-t-elle. La qualité des produits et la possibilité de proposer des vêtements à des prix abordables constituent aussi des atouts pour les revendeurs. « En plus de la qualité, c’est moins cher. Cela nous arrange, nous les revendeurs, parce qu’on peut facilement revendre à des prix abordables sans que le client ne s’en plaigne », ajoute Marie Renée Sylla. Coudre et transformer sur place : le visage du consommer local À quelques pas des étals, l’ambiance change. Aux discussions animées des commerçants succède le vrombissement régulier des machines à coudre. Dans les ateliers voisins, chaque espace est mis à profit. Sur les tables de repassage, de jeunes employés s’appliquent à donner leur finition aux tenues. À proximité, des artisans tracent les contours des modèles à la craie avant de découper les tissus à grands coups de ciseaux. Le mètre ruban autour du cou, prêt à prendre les mesures d’un client, le couturier Boubacar Kâ suit attentivement le travail en cours. Il apprécie la qualité et la diversité des étoffes disponibles sur le marché. « Il y a des tissus très jolis et de très bonne qualité », affirme-t-il. Pour cet artisan, le recours aux tissus vendus à Colobane donne tout son sens à la complémentarité entre commerce et confection. « Les tissus que l’on coud viennent d’ici même, de Colobane. Parfois, on propose différents tissus au client, et c’est à lui de voir ce qui lui convient », explique-t-il. Sa clientèle est composée de particuliers, mais aussi de professionnels de la mode. « La plupart de mes clients achètent des tissus et viennent les faire coudre chez moi. Nous travaillons très souvent pour des stylistes qui font de la vente en ligne », précise-t-il. Du commerce des étoffes à la confection sur mesure, le marché Gambie et les ateliers de Colobane font ainsi vivre un réseau d’acteurs complémentaires. Commerçants, couturiers, créateurs et vendeurs en ligne participent à une économie de proximité qui soutient l’emploi et valorise les préférences vestimentaires locales. Cette dynamique montre que le consommer local ne se limite pas à un slogan. Il repose aussi sur des pratiques quotidiennes, des savoir-faire et des circuits commerciaux qui rapprochent fournisseurs, artisans et consommateurs. Un potentiel qui pourrait contribuer davantage à la valorisation de la mode sénégalaise et au renforcement de son tissu économique. Fatou NGOM

items.title: Joyce Bawah Mogtari says Obaasima Conference should help women connect and learn
items.description: Senior Presidential Advisor and Aide to President John Dramani Mahama, Joyce Bawah Mogtari, has called for the Obaasima Conference to serve as a space where women can openly discuss their leadership experiences, learn from one another and build relationships that strengthen their professional and personal development. In a Facebook post on Friday, October 16, she reflected on a conversation with former Electoral Commission Chairperson Charlotte Osei, whose account of the challenges of being a woman in leadership prompted her to consider the value of shared experiences and mutual support. Ms Bawah Mogtari said the discussion highlighted the pressures women may face, from rumours and workplace prejudice to colleagues who question their ability to handle responsibilities. She said creating opportunities for women to discuss such experiences openly could help them find practical ways to navigate difficult working environments and encourage one another. She identified the importance of finding a supportive circle of people who will offer honest counsel, stand against unfair treatment and celebrate each other’s achievements. According to Ms Bawah Mogtari, that spirit of connection and solidarity should be central to the Obaasima Conference, enabling women not only to exchange ideas but also to build lasting networks of support.

items.title: El FMI advierte de que el “mediocre crecimiento” de la zona euro se prolongará a medio plazo
items.description: En contra de los vaticinios más negativos, en el último año la zona euro ha resistido los varapalos financieros de la geopolítica internacional. Prueba de ello es que el Fondo Monetario Internacional (FMI) prevé que el PIB avance un 1,1% en 2026 (dos décimas más que en su revisión de junio), tras repuntar un 1,5% en 2025 y un 0,9% en 2024. El dato apunta a una economía más resistente de lo que cabría esperar ante el deterioro del entorno internacional, pero también pone de manifiesto el problema que el organismo identifica para los próximos años: aunque la región crece, no tiene suficiente potencial para hacerlo a un ritmo mayor. items.title: Don’t Let Big Tech Dictate Humanity’s Future
items.description: Should human beings remain in control of planet Earth? Or should we be replaced as the dominant species? As absurd as these questions may sound, and as obvious as the answers may seem, the Big Tech oligarchs funding the artificial-intelligence revolution have responded in ways that should alarm all of us. In Silicon Valley, some of the wealthiest people on Earth believe that they have the power to create a superior species. Sam Altman, the head of OpenAI, wrote in 2017 that AI would allow humans to become “the first species ever to design our own descendants.” What this means for humans, however, remains unclear. According to Altman, we will either jump-start digital intelligence “and then fade into an evolutionary tree branch, or we can figure out what a successful merge looks like.” In other words, humans have a choice: face extinction or merge with machines. “I believe the merge has already started,” Altman added, and is “probably our best-case scenario.” Similarly, Dario Amodei, the head of Anthropic, has opened up the possibility of rights for AI models. “We don’t know if the models are conscious,” he explained , and added, “But we’re open to the idea that it could be.” Earlier this month, Elon Musk, the head of SpaceXAI and the richest man on Earth, posted on X, “Propagating super intelligence to the stars is a great success condition for a biological bootloader,” likening humans to the programming that launches a computer’s operating system. Put simply, Musk is saying that humans are merely a step toward digital superintelligence. Peter Thiel, the billionaire co-founder of Palantir and a major AI investor, was asked last year if he would prefer that the human race endure. His response ? “Uh … Well, I don’t know. I would—I would … There’s so many questions implicit in this,” he stammered, before reluctantly conceding that humans should survive. [ Read: AI companies’ new plan to keep themselves from destroying everything ] These views are rooted in a once-fringe Silicon Valley ideology called “ transhumanism .” Transhumanists believe that technology will allow us to transcend humanity either by creating a new species or by combining ourselves with machines. Why go beyond humans? Because these new “posthumans” will be smarter than us. They will be infallible. They will go to the stars and conquer the universe. They will live forever. If these were the fantasies of teenage boys obsessed with science fiction, we could laugh them off. They are not. These are the foundational beliefs of the most powerful people in the world, who are mobilizing trillions of dollars to turn them into reality. And these investments are already paying off. For tens of thousands of years, humans had a monopoly on language. Only we could use sentences. No longer. For thousands of years, humans were the only ones capable of solving complex problems in fields such as mathematics. No longer. Until recently, we could reliably tell when a human, as opposed to a computer, was talking to us through a screen. No longer. Machines are , in fact, already beginning to replace us. And the vision Big Tech oligarchs have for the future gets only more frightening. Musk is building Neuralink to implant chips in people’s brains in order to achieve a “symbiosis with artificial intelligence.” Thiel has decamped to Argentina, where President Javier Milei has called for the establishment of “non-human corporations” operated by AI agents, for which “human shareholders may participate, but are not required.” An Anthropic co-founder, Christopher Olah, has been trying to convince religious leaders, including the pope, that AI could be conscious. This is absurd. This is irresponsible. And almost no one outside Silicon Valley wants this future. There is a reason why 91 percent of Americans think we need guardrails on AI, why 74 percent do not trust the leaders of AI companies, and why 73 percent are concerned AI could threaten human survival. [ Read: AI is running laps around our political system ] In May, Pope Leo XIV released his first encyclical, Magnificent Humanity , in which he warned against an “anti-human vision” whereby “the human person risks being reduced to data, a cog in a machine or a commodity.” The pope was clear: “Humanity—in all its grandeur and woundedness—must never be replaced or surpassed.” In response, Thiel called the pope “a Chinese Communist agent.” But the pope was right. Thiel and his fellow Big Tech oligarchs could not be more wrong. Humanity must not allow a handful of multibillionaires to recklessly attempt to replace us. We must place an immediate pause on advanced-AI development and ban artificial superintelligence—an artificial mind smarter than any human, capable of operating independently beyond our control—until a new federal body is able to ensure the technology’s safety. That’s why I have introduced legislation with Representative Greg Casar to do just that. AI is an existential threat to humanity. It must be treated as such. The future of humanity cannot be left in the hands of a few Big Tech oligarchs who are obsessed with money and power. The American people and people throughout the world must determine that future. Human beings, not machines, must come first.

items.title: PHC to hear PTI chairman’s plea against emergency, governor’s rule in KP on Oct 20
items.description: PESHAWAR: The Peshawar High Court on Friday fixed October 20 for the preliminary hearing of a petition filed by PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan challenging the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and seeking to have the move declared unconstitutional. The federal government on October 11 imposed emergency in KP, and placed the province under governor’s rule, taking note of the “provincial government’s deliberate disengagement from the fight against terrorism”. The move followed weeks of political tensions between the Centre and the PTI — as well as negotiations to bridge their differences — after the latter announced a long march to Islamabad to demand the release of its jailed founder, Imran Khan. The opposition had criticised the move, vowing to raise its voice at every forum, including the judiciary. The instant petition was filed on October 14 by the PTI chairman . He will be represented by a panel of lawyers, including Barrister Sameer Khosa, Salman Akram Raja, Ali Zaman, Sardar Haseeb Ahmad and Zainab Shahid. The members of the bench that will hear the petition will be announced later. In his petition, Gohar urged the PHC to declare the federal government’s decision to impose emergency and governor’s rule in KP “unconstitutional, ultra vires, coram non judice, tainted with malice in law and fact, devoid of objective material, and of no legal effect” and to set aside the proclamation. Filed under Article 199 of the Constitution, the petition named the federation of Pakistan (through the secretaries of the Cabinet Division, law, interior, and defence ministries); the province of KP; KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi; the KP Assembly speaker; and the secretary of the KP Home and Tribal Affairs Department as respondents. Sohail Afridi, who is no longer functioning as the province’s chief minister following the imposition of governor’s rule, was also named as a pro forma respondent. Gohar challenged the “constitutionality, legality and vires” of the October 11 decision, the order deploying army troops to the province, and “all consequential and derivative executive orders, notifications, and bodies” constituted as a result. These included the establishment of the KP Advisory Council and the “arbitrary” detention and removal of Afridi as the lawful chief minister of KP, along with his provincial cabinet, which had been vested with full executive powers under Article 130 of the Constitution. Following the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in the province, the federal government formed an 11-member technocratic KP Advisory Council. The council will assist Governor Kundi, who is now in charge of running the province, in exercising the functions of the KP government on behalf of the federal government. The PHC was further requested to declare that Paragraph 2 of the proclamation — which transferred the legislative powers of the KP Assembly to Parliament in the absence of a prior resolution passed by the assembly, as required under Article 232(1) — was “void ab initio and an unconstitutional usurpation of provincial autonomy”. The petition also urged the PHC to restrain the federation from “tabling, entertaining, or enacting any provincial legislative business concerning Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in Parliament”. The petitioner asked the court to declare the proclamation illegal and unconstitutional and to set aside, dissolve or permanently restrain all executive orders, notifications, actions and bodies created “pursuant to or under the colour of” the proclamation. These included the constitution of the 11-member KP Advisory Council, headed by Governor Kundi; the establishment of the Area Development Secretariat (ADS) across 12 districts of the province; and the removal of the KP advocate general and the purported appointment of a replacement. The ADS was established to “restore law and order, safeguard the security of the citizens of Pakistan and ensure good governance and development” in Dera Ismail Khan, Tank, Lakki Marwat, Bannu, Bajaur, Mohmand, Khyber, Kurram, Orakzai, North Waziristan, South Waziristan (Upper) and South Waziristan (Lower). The petitioner also challenged the October 11 order deploying army troops under Article 245, asking the court to declare it unconstitutional on the grounds that it could not “supplant or bypass the civilian executive and constitutional administration” of the province and could not be invoked in the absence of a lawful requisition by the provincial government headed by Afridi. Gohar sought directives requiring the respondents, including the federal government and the KP governor, to immediately disclose, produce and place before the PHC “the entire record and so-called ‘objective material’”, including Governor Kundi’s report and the federal cabinet’s summary, on which the emergency proclamation and subsequent orders were allegedly based. He also sought directives for the immediate release of Afridi and members of the KP cabinet and assembly from “unlawful executive or preventive detention”. The petition further urged the court to direct the respondents to immediately produce Afridi before the PHC and restrain the state from placing him or any cabinet members in preventive detention or transferring them outside the court’s jurisdiction. The petition claimed that, by unilaterally bypassing the elected provincial assembly over an alleged question of internal disturbance, the impugned proclamation violated “the federal structure guaranteed under Article 1, the principles of democracy and provincial autonomy enshrined in the Objectives Resolution (Article 2A), and the legislative domain of the province recognised by Article 142 of the Constitution”. On these grounds, the proclamation was “ultra vires the proviso to Article 232(1) read with Article 1, 2A, and 142 of the Constitution” and liable to be set aside, it added. Gohar further contended that the proclamation made no mention of any “grave emergency” arising from a war or other external aggression, as required by the text of Article 232(1) — nor would such an assertion be supported by facts. He maintained that neither the country nor KP faced a grave emergency from any ongoing war or external aggression, nor was there any known risk or threat of such. The petition further contended that the reliance on “internal disturbances” in the province needed to be assessed against a demonstrable and objective criterion, which was “entirely absent” from the impugned proclamation. “Despite an unfortunately high number of incidents of terrorist violence in Balochistan, no state of emergency has been declared or even contemplated,” the petition stated. “This clearly demonstrates that the terrorism and security pretext in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa is nothing but a colourable device, deployed in sheer violation of Article 25.” The petition alleged that this pretext had been used solely because the KP government was formed by the opposition and its demands regarding PTI founder Imran Khan were unacceptable to the federal government. It added that the federal government’s claim was also belied by the fact that even at the height of terrorism between 2007 and 2015, “no emergency was ever imposed anywhere inside Pakistan”. Gohar also argued that the invocation of Article 234 was “without lawful authority, tainted with malice in law, and devoid of jurisdictional basis”. NDM petition Another petition challenging the imposition of emergency, filed by National Democratic Movement (NDM) central and provincial presidents Mohsin Dawar and Bushra Gohar, respectively, has also been fixed for hearing on October 20. The joint petition stated that the proclamation of emergency and governor’s rule was “purely and patently against the mandate of people of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, hence, liable to be set at naught”. The petitioners prayed that the court declare the proclamation issued by the president of Pakistan on October 11, 2026, to be without legal effect and jurisdiction. They also requested the court to set aside the directions, appointments and actions taken, as well as omissions made, pursuant to the proclamation, to ensure constitutional conformity. They further sought interim relief, asking the court to suspend the operation of the impugned presidential proclamation until the final disposal of the writ petition. The petitioners stated that the president of Pakistan was under a solemn constitutional duty, under Article 42 of the Constitution read with the Third Schedule, to preserve, protect and defend the Constitution and not allow personal interests to influence official conduct or decisions. They claimed that the KP governor, acting with mala fide intent and without jurisdiction, submitted a tailor-made report to the president of Pakistan. They alleged that, without taking into account the constitutional guidelines explicitly set out in Articles 232 and 234 of the Constitution of Pakistan, 1973, the respondents issued the impugned proclamation on October 11, 2026. The petitioners contended that the KP government and its executive had never reported the respondent emergency call/whistle blow regarding the security concern, which was beyond the control of the government; hence, the action and issuance of the proclamation solely and exclusively by the president was against the norms and contours of democracy and provincial autonomy. They added that the issuance of the proclamation was the outcome of mala fide, and patently without jurisdiction and had no constitutional backing. They further contended that Article 232 of the Constitution had delineated a specific procedure and limitations for declaring and proclamation of emergency in the province, which had not been followed by the respondents; hence, the action and orders of “Proclamation of Emergency” in the province of KP were unconstitutional and unlawful.

items.title: Imaan, Hadi walk out of proceedings after objecting to jail trial in security breach case
items.description: RAWALPINDI: Rights activist and lawyer Imaan Zainab Mazari-Hazir and her husband, Hadi Ali Chattha, on Friday objected to the manner of their presentation during the hearing of the security breach case, with the couple and their lawyers eventually walking out of the proceedings at Adiala jail. The defence counsel also filed an application seeking an end to the jail trial. The case pertains to the alleged disruption of a security route of an international cricket team and incitement to public unrest. Imaan and her husband have been accused of removing barriers from the route. The couple was indicted in the case on Oct 7. A day earlier, at the police’s recommendation, citing limitations in transporting the accused to court, the court directed counsels and witnesses to appear at the Adiala jail for the next hearing. On Friday, Anti-Terrorism Court (ATC) Judge Tahir Abbas Sipra conducted the hearing inside Adiala jail, where proceedings commenced at 10:55am, according to the defence counsel present inside the makeshift courtroom. The accused were presented inside a dock located in a corner of the courtroom, prompting them to raise objections over the manner in which they were produced before the court. “This is not the proper way to present someone in court,” Imaan said, adding that they were not being allowed to meet their lawyers. Hadi complained that the two were being treated worse than terrorists. Judge Sipra, taking note of the police standing next to the accused, directed the personnel to move away and remarked: “They have been brought into the courtroom; what is the need for the police to stand right next to them?” The defence counsel had also filed an application seeking an end to the jail trial and adjournment of the hearing on Friday. After hearing arguments from the lawyers, the court announced a 20-minute recess. On the application filed by the defence, he said, “I have received your applications; I will issue an order regarding this.” After the proceedings resumed, prosecution witness Ibrahim recorded his statement, while defence lawyer Aimal Khan Mandokhail urged the court to decide the application seeking adjournment before proceeding further. “We have filed an application to adjourn the hearing; please rule on it,” he told the court. He also complained that other members of the defence legal team were not being allowed to enter the courtroom. “If the proceedings continue in this manner, we cannot remain a part of them,” Mandokhail said. He further urged the court to not defer the matter until the following day, referring to the pending bail proceedings. Subsequently, Imaan, Hadi and their lawyers walked out of the courtroom. Imaan and Hadi’s rearrest The lawyer couple has been in jail since their arrest on Jan 23 in a case registered against them for protesting outside the Islamabad High Court and allegedly manhandling the IHC Bar Association president. The arrest prompted criticism by rights bodies, politicians and journalists, who stressed the couple’s right to a fair trial. Just a day later, a sessions court sentenced them to 17 years on multiple charges under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca) in a case pertaining to controversial social media posts. The convictions were widely condemned by lawyers and United Nations (UN) experts . On Sept 17, following months of litigation before the courts , the Supreme Court suspended their sentences in the case. The SC ordered their release pending the Islamabad High Court’s final verdict on their appeals against the trial court’s decision. However, the reprieve was short-lived as hours later, Islamabad police arrested the couple again in connection with another case and produced them before an ATC, which sent them to jail on judicial remand. The fresh case in which the two were arrested was registered at the federal capital’s Kohsar police station on March 22 last year on the complaint of City Magistrate Ghulam Murtaza Chandio. Imaan and Hadi were accused of chanting anti-government slogans and blocking roads and were nominated by name in the FIR. However, at the time of registration of the case, no section of the Anti-Terrorism Act (ATA) had been added. The FIR included sections 188 (disobedience of an order lawfully promulgated by a public servant), 341 (wrongful restraint), 506 (punishment for criminal intimidation), 353 (assault or use of criminal force to deter a public servant from discharging their official duty) and 186 (obstructing a public servant in the performance of official duties).

Journée mondiale de la normalisation 2026 : L’ABNORM sensibilise des étudiants, des acteurs économiques et institutionnels sur la qualité et le respect des normes à Dédougou, région de Bankui
items.description: La secrétaire générale de la région de Bankui , Adjara Kientega, a présidé la commémoration de la Journée mondiale de la normalisation (JMN), édition 2026, le 14 octobre à Dédougou. L’Agence burkinabè de normalisation, de la métrologie et de la qualité (ABNORM) est l’organisatrice de la cérémonie, articulée autour de deux activités principales : un séminaire d’information et de sensibilisation des acteurs socio-économiques et institutionnels locaux, et une conférence-débat avec les étudiants de l’Université Daniel-Ouezzin-Coulibaly sur les enjeux de la normalisation pour le développement du Burkina Faso. Du 14 au 15 octobre 2026, l’Agence burkinabè de normalisation, de la métrologie et de la qualité (ABNORM) a célébré à Dédougou, dans la région de la Boucle du Mouhoun, l’édition 2026 de la Journée mondiale de la normalisation (JMN) sous le thème « Une vision commune pour un monde meilleur ». La date du 14 octobre de chaque année étant dédiée à la reconnaissance et à la valorisation des activités de normalisation à travers le monde, l’ABNORM a saisi l’occasion cette année pour se rendre à Dédougou à la rencontre des acteurs régionaux afin de magnifier l’événement autour d’activités d’information, de sensibilisation et d’échanges. L’ouverture des travaux est intervenue dans la matinée du mercredi 14 octobre 2026, sous la présidence de la secrétaire générale de la région, Adjara Kientega, représentant le gouverneur. Étaient également présentes des autorités administratives, militaires et paramilitaires, des notabilités coutumières et religieuses, des acteurs économiques et industriels de la région, ainsi que le directeur régional de l’ABNORM du Guiriko, Prosper Sidnoma Moubarack Ouédraogo, représentant le directeur général de la structure. La commémoration de cette journée vise la reconnaissance de l’expertise des acteurs impliqués dans les activités de normalisation, a confié le directeur de la normalisation et de la certification à l’ABNORM, Dr Alain Gustave Yaguibou. « C’est bon de marquer un arrêt pour valoriser la contribution d’éminents experts qui nous permettent de commercer, de pénétrer le marché et de consommer des produits sans problème », a-t-il déclaré. Le chargé de la certification a expliqué que, depuis la création de l’ABNORM, plus de 1 400 normes ont été élaborées, couvrant une grande diversité de produits burkinabè. Dans la même dynamique, des certificats ont été délivrés pour matérialiser la conformité de près de 1 600 produits nationaux aux normes, a-t-il ajouté. La commémoration de la JMN 2026 s’est articulée autour de communications visant à informer et sensibiliser les acteurs socio-économiques et industriels, les producteurs et les acteurs institutionnels locaux sur l’application des normes, la maîtrise des procédés de production et de transformation, ainsi que sur le respect des exigences de qualité et de sécurité. L’objectif est de permettre aux produits transformés dans les différentes unités de répondre aux attentes des consommateurs et d’accéder durablement au marché, tout en offrant des garanties de confiance. Moderniser l’économie Voir l’ABNORM dans la région de la Boucle du Mouhoun, au contact des forces vives, pour commémorer la journée du 14 octobre est une initiative et une démarche très appréciées. Gérant de station à Dédougou, Abdoul Aziz Gansonré a soutenu que le séminaire d’information et de sensibilisation a permis aux participants de découvrir l’ABNORM et son mode de fonctionnement. « Nous avons été informés et sensibilisés sur les exigences à remplir pour être en conformité avec les normes établies, sans oublier les informations sur la documentation à détenir », a-t-il relevé. En plus du séminaire, l’ABNORM a eu des échanges avec les étudiants de l’Université Daniel-Ouezzin-Coulibaly de Dédougou, le 15 octobre 2026, autour d’une conférence-débat sur le thème « Normalisation et certification : outils stratégiques pour l’innovation locale et la compétitivité internationale ». Cette activité a eu pour ambition de rapprocher la normalisation du monde universitaire, de susciter l’intérêt des futurs ingénieurs, chercheurs, entrepreneurs et techniciens, et de favoriser une meilleure prise en compte des exigences de qualité dans les projets. Quant à la présidente de la cérémonie, Adjara Kientega, elle a indiqué que la normalisation contribue à la modernisation de l’économie et à l’amélioration des conditions de vie des populations. C’est ainsi que le gouvernement, à travers l’ABNORM, accorde une importance particulière à la qualité en accompagnant les opérateurs économiques dans leurs efforts d’amélioration qualitative des produits et de protection des consommateurs. Il s’agit, selon elle, de faire de la qualité un levier de compétitivité, de création de valeur et de souveraineté économique. Elle a poursuivi en soulignant que la normalisation constitue un instrument de prévention des risques et d’amélioration des performances. « Elle permet aux entreprises de disposer de références techniques communes, d’améliorer leurs procédés de production et de répondre plus efficacement aux attentes des marchés. Elle favorise également l’innovation en facilitant la diffusion des connaissances techniques et l’adoption de solutions éprouvées », a soutenu la secrétaire générale régionale. Yacouba BELEM

I still can’t wrap my head around this. It hurts, but I will not sorrow as those who have no hope. “I find comfort in knowing that a saint has joined the angels. “Toluwanisings, rest on, dear one, in the bosom of your Lord. “May God comfort and strengthen your family, friends, and colleagues. items.title: AI is coming for every company, says Nvidia boss
items.description: Artificial intelligence will ultimately become a key aspect of all companies, the head of AI chip giant Nvidia said during a visit to Stockholm, where he urged Europe to ramp up its AI industry. “Every single company will be an AI company eventually. Every single industry will be impacted by AI,” Jensen Huang told an event late Thursday, part of a European tour that includes a Nvidia-hosted conference in Berlin next week. “The important thing for us is to recognise that Europe needs to build out the entire stack,” he said, referring to the AI technology chain from data centres to chatbots and other apps. Speaking later to AFP, Huang said his company had invested $8 billion in Europe over the past year. “We’ve strategically invested in different parts of that ecosystem, really high quality companies that we believe could help lift it, the whole ecosystem in Europe,” he said, citing the British data centre and AI cloud provider Nscale and the Dutch cloud provider Nebius as examples. “In the last one year, we’ve invested $8 billion already. We have another couple of billion dollars in the pipeline,” he added. “We’re helping Europe create the AI ecosystem.” Huang was in Stockholm for the launch of Sferical One, a Swedish supercomputer using Nvidia chips that will keep sensitive Swedish data and expertise in the country. During his visit, Volvo Cars also announced it was expanding its partnership with Nvidia to improve safety technology in its planned self-driving vehicles.
